title: Friends
hookLine: a friend loves at all times (Proverbs 17:17)
tomorrow: is your neighbor everyone on earth, or the person next door?

lines: A FRIEND LOVETH AT ALL TIMES.
cards: Two sayings from the same book, a few pages apart. One: “A friend loveth at all times.” The other: “Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.”
Wounds, faithful? Kisses, deceitful? Some friendships run on the opposite rule: hype each other up, never say the hard thing.
So which is it in Proverbs: the friend who always loves, or the friend who wounds?

teach.b: It's the same friend. Look at the whole first line: “A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.” At all times: the good days, the long ordinary middle, and the day something has to be said.
A friend who only flatters loves at some times. The wound is faithful because it's honest, and because it comes from someone who's staying.
Flattery costs nothing; honesty risks the friendship, and a friend takes that risk.
Proverbs also notices that friendship takes work: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

Then, at supper on his last night, Jesus takes the word for himself: “Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.”
In John's telling, a friend is someone you let in and tell the truth to. Here's one to repeat tonight: the same book that praises a friend's love praises a friend's wounds, and sees no contradiction.
So at all times includes two hard things: hearing the honest word, and saying the true, kind one back.

how: Christians often see friendship as part of faith, since Jesus calls his disciples friends; some pray for friends by name, and some churches value spiritual friendship, where friends help each other grow.

o: people who love at all times, honest words included
people you see often and enjoy spending time with
classmates or coworkers you happen to know well

games.q: friends in Proverbs and John — tap the pairs.
p: Jesus at supper, his last night

s: a friend who loves at all times never says anything that hurts
the same book says faithful are the wounds of a friend.
Proverbs says a man that hath friends must shew himself friendly
in John, Jesus calls his disciples servants to the end
"I call you not servants … but I have called you friends."

games.q: your friend is about to text her ex something she'll regret, and asks you to say it's a great idea. what does 'at all times' look like?
o: hype her up; a friend always agrees.
tell her honestly, and kindly, what you think.
stay out of it; it's not your business.
games.why: faithful are the wounds of a friend. loving at all times includes the honest word, said kindly, by someone who's staying.

practice: Bring one friend to mind: someone who has been there at all times, or once told you a hard truth you needed. Say their name quietly, and one thing they mean to you, as if they could hear it. If you pray, thank God for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Friends. People who love at all times: the good days, the ordinary ones, and the day something hard has to be said.

orig.note: Greek: friend; in John 15:15 Jesus says, I have called you friends.

carryVoice: The line to keep: at all times, the honest words and the staying included. See you tomorrow.
